subject: Data Engineering
title: Who Owns Data Quality?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Who Owns Data Quality?.

hook.text: The dashboard shows wrong numbers. Analytics blames engineering. Engineering blames the source team.

buildup.text: Data quality fails when nobody owns it. Everyone assumes someone else will catch the errors.

discovery.text: Ownership means a named person or team is accountable for each dataset's quality and freshness.

twist.text: Producers should own quality at the source. Consumers should own validation at the point of use.

climax.text: Shared responsibility works only when the handoff is explicit — documented in a data contract.

punchline.text: If everyone owns it, nobody owns it.

quiz.question: What is the biggest cause of data quality failures in organizations?
options: No clear ownership of data quality
